newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks consolidate lower, Hanbo watched.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks consolidate lower, Hanbo watched.

text.p: Stocks crept lower on Saturday as investors started taking profits across the board in the belief the market has reached its top for the time being, brokers said.
They said shares were likely to go through further consolidation early next week.
The composite stock index stood at 683.13 at the close, down 2.71 points from Friday. Declining issues beat advancers by 533 to 243.
Brokers said the market was still cautious over further fall-out from the Hanbo crisis, but said the issue didn't have much impact on trading today.
"The market is in for consolidation after three straight days of gains," said Baek Jung-hyun of Samsung Securities.
"The Hanbo scandal didn't have much impact because it has been already reflected in the market," said Baek.
Hanbo Steel, the conglomerate's flagship, is seeking court receivership after piling up almost five trillion won in loans.
The government has supplied more than three trillion won into the money market since last week to ease a financial squeeze caused by Hanbo's failure.
Hanbo Steel shares, currently under the watch list, fell to their daily limit low of 3,030, down 260 won.
Volume totalled 21.51 million shares in half-session trading on Saturday, compared with 31.99 million on Friday.
